question: to the Commission Lynn Boylan (The Left), Vicent Marzà Ibáñez (Verts/ALE), Estrella Galán (The Left), Vladimir Prebilič (Verts/ALE), Per Clausen (The Left), Martin Günther (The Left), Oihane Agirregoitia Martínez (Renew), Andreas Schieder (S&D), Isabel Serra Sánchez (The Left), Irene Montero (The Left), Rudi Kennes (The Left), Kathleen Funchion (The Left), Jaume Asens Llodrà (Verts/ALE), João Oliveira (The Left) Subject:

The EU-based airline Ryanair has recently launched an email campaign advertising routes to Dakhla in the non-self governing territory of Western Sahara. The advertisement describes visiting Dakhla as part of a Moroccan adventure and on their website lists the city as ‘Morocco’s best kept secret’1. Several times the advertisement describes Dakhla as Moroccan and makes no reference to Western Sahara or the Sahrawi people. Dakhla is part of the non-self governing territory of Western Sahara, occupied by Morocco since 1975. The International Court of Justice confirmed2 that this territory does not belong to Morocco and it is listed on the United Nations list of non-self governing territories3. In response to a previous question4, the Commission informed airlines that the EuroMediterranean aviation agreement between the EU and Morocco does not apply to Western Sahara. However, Ryanair are still engaging in practices designed to deceive EU consumers. Will the Commission: 1.
Instruct airlines to not advertise a destination as belonging to an occupying power, thereby erasing the presence of the indigenous people?
Instruct Ryanair to cease these deceptive advertising practices?
Issue guidance for airlines operating in the EU regarding their obligations in respect of non-self governing territories?

https://www.ryanair.com/ie/en/lp/explore/morocco. https://www.icj-cij.org/sites/default/files/case-related/61/061-19751016-ADV-01-00-EN.pdf. https://www.un.org/dppa/decolonization/en/nsgt. https://www.europarl.europa.eu/doceo/document/E-10-2024-002585_EN.html.
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (25.6.2026) As mentioned in its reply to parliamentary question E-002585/2024, the Commission has already informed EU carriers that, in accordance with the case law of the Court of Justice, the Euro-Mediterranean aviation agreement between the EU and Morocco does not apply to routes to the territory of the Western Sahara. This means that carriers are not bound by the provisions of said agreement, including concerning the operation and the advertisement of routes from the EU to Western Sahara and vice versa. Furthermore: 1. The Commission cannot issue general instructions to air carriers on how to describe territorial sovereignty in commercial communications. However, EU-established airlines must comply with EU consumer-protection law, including Directives 2005/29/EC1 and 2006/114/EC2, which prohibit misleading actions or omissions likely to affect the average consumer’s transactional decision. Presenting a destination in a way that misleads consumers about a territory’s status may therefore raise issues under those rules. 2. The enforcement of EU consumer-protection law in individual cases is primarily the responsibility of national competent authorities and courts in the Member States. The Commission therefore cannot substitute itself for national enforcement authorities by ordering a specific company to cease a given practice. 3.The Commission takes note of the concerns raised and will continue to monitor the correct application of EU consumer-protection law in the aviation sector.
